body:
Fixes the bug reported on the forum: https://qelectrotech.org/forum/viewtopic.php?id=3125

## Problem

Using "Export the names of list of wires" (`ConductorNumExport`), a single named conductor was exported twice. Reporter's exact words: *"I have a name conductor named '16AWG' and when I use this command it exports two of the same so: '16AWG' '16AWG'"*.

## Root cause

`ConductorNumExport::fillHash()` incremented the name's tally once per **terminal** instead of once per **conductor** — a separate `if` block for `terminal1` and another for `terminal2`, each independently bumping the same `m_hash` entry. Since an ordinary conductor has two terminals and neither is a folio-report terminal in the common case, both blocks fired and every real conductor was counted twice. `wiresNum()` then faithfully repeats each name `m_hash.value(key)` times, so the doubled count became doubled output lines. No bus, multiple diagrams, or master/slave elements needed — a single ordinary two-terminal named conductor reproduces it every time.

## Fix

Increment once per conductor, skipping it only when *both* ends are folio-report terminals (neither represents a real connection) instead of checking each terminal independently and incrementing twice.

## Testing

Verified with a minimal two-conductor project via the `--export-wires` CLI verb:
- **Before fix:** 2 named conductors → 4 lines exported (exact doubling from the report)
- **After fix:** 2 named conductors → 2 lines exported (correct)

Also did a clean incremental build with no errors/new warnings.

of list of wires" doubled every conductor's name in the output - a
single conductor named "16AWG" was exported as two "16AWG" lines.

Root cause: ConductorNumExport::fillHash() incremented the name's
tally once per terminal instead of once per conductor - a separate
if-block for terminal1 and another for terminal2, each bumping the
same m_hash entry. Since an ordinary conductor has two terminals and
neither is a folio-report terminal in the common case, both blocks
fired and every real conductor was counted twice. wiresNum() then
faithfully repeats each name m_hash.value(key) times, so the doubled
count became doubled output lines.

Fixed by incrementing once per conductor, only skipping it entirely
when *both* ends are folio-report terminals (neither represents a
real connection) rather than checking each terminal independently.

Verified with a minimal two-conductor project via the --export-wires
CLI verb: pre-fix build produced 4 lines for 2 named conductors
(exact doubling), post-fix build produces the correct 2.
